caveats: **`head`'s declared result columns don't match what the code emits.** The definition YAML declares `status|content_length|content_type`; `do_head` actually writes `status|headers`, where `headers` is the full raw header block. A consumer parsing by the declared schema will not find `content_length`/`content_type`.

**`get`'s size cap doesn't stop the transfer.** `download` aborts mid-transfer past 100 MiB (its content receiver counts the buffered bytes). `get` calls `cli.Get(parsed.path)` with no content receiver, so the full body is already downloaded in memory before the `res->body.size() > kMaxDownloadSize` check replaces it with an error string — the cap limits what's returned, not what's fetched. `download` holds the whole body in memory (up to 100 MiB, reserved once from `Content-Length` when declared) before writing, and reports an allocation failure as `download aborted: out of memory`.

**No redirect following.** Neither `set_follow_location` nor any equivalent is called on any `httplib::Client`/`SSLClient` instance, so for `get` and `head` a 3xx response is returned as-is (status + whatever body/headers the redirect response itself carries), not followed; for `download` anything but a 2xx status is a failure (`download failed: HTTP <status>`) and writes nothing.

**HTTPS on Windows depends on a build-time OpenSSL find.** Windows OpenSSL discovery is `required: false` (`meson.build`); when it isn't found, `CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT` is undefined and every `https://` call on that build returns `status|0` with an "HTTPS not supported" message instead of connecting (lines 283-287, 334-337, 378-381). Linux/macOS require OpenSSL at configure time and always have it.

**This plugin does not set a typed result status.** Every sample shows `UNDECLARED / UNKNOWN /` regardless of outcome — a caller must parse the `status`/`error` output fields, not the result-status envelope, to detect failure.

definitions.description: Download a file from a URL to a local path with optional SHA256 hash verification.
Perform an HTTP GET request and return the response status and body.
Perform an HTTP HEAD request and return the response status code and headers. Useful for checking file availability or size before downloading.

description: HTTP client — download files, GET/HEAD requests with hash verification (no shell-out)
how_it_works: All three actions parse the operator-supplied URL, reject anything but `http://`/`https://`, and vet the destination before opening a connection (`agents/shared/outbound_address_policy.hpp`): the host name is resolved **once**, every address the lookup returned must be a public address, and the connection goes to one of those vetted addresses (IPv4 first, then IPv6, each tried in turn) through cpp-httplib's hostname-to-address map, so the `Host` header and TLS name verification stay on the original name and a DNS answer that changes between the check and the connect cannot redirect it. Loopback, private (RFC 1918, carrier-grade NAT, unique-local), link-local and the cloud metadata addresses (`169.254.169.254`, `168.63.129.16`, the Alibaba Cloud metadata address, `fd00:ec2::254`), unspecified, multicast, reserved, documentation and other non-global blocks are refused, IPv4-mapped, NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96`) and 6to4 forms are judged by the IPv4 address they embed, and a failed lookup blocks the request (fail closed). `get` and `head` then issue a single GET or HEAD under a 120 s total deadline and return the status plus body/headers as-is, except that `get` returns at most the first 1 MiB of the body: a longer body is cut there and a final `truncated|1048576` row follows the `body` row (the status is still the peer's), so one `get` result can never be a frame the server refuses. Use `download` for a larger body. `download` first refuses a destination on a network or device path (or whose resolved parent is one) and any path containing a `..` component, then fetches the body into memory (capped at 100 MiB, 600 s total deadline) accepting only a **2xx** status, requires the body to be **complete** (it matches `Content-Length`, or the framing is chunked, or an `expected_hash` is given to verify it; a body with none of these is refused because a cut-short close-delimited transfer cannot be told from a finished one), checks `expected_hash` (case-insensitive SHA-256) and only then replaces the destination in one atomic rename. A failed, non-2xx, over-cap, incomplete or unverified transfer writes nothing and leaves an existing destination as it was; the replacement is a new regular file, so a symlink or hard-linked destination is replaced rather than written through. Every request goes through cpp-httplib's native in-process socket client, no shell invocation on any platform. The plugin deliberately does not follow HTTP redirects, does not accept custom headers/methods/auth, and does not retry a failed request. It also never decodes a compressed response: every client turns httplib's response decompression off (`set_decompress(false)`), so `download` hashes and stores exactly the bytes the peer sent, and `get` and `head` ask for `identity` encoding and return whatever arrives undecoded. A host that answers both IPv4 and IPv6 is tried address by address (IPv4 first, at most four addresses, one total deadline for all attempts) and only a failure to connect moves on to the next address. `download` stores exactly the bytes it received (a gzip body is stored compressed and `expected_hash` is compared with those stored bytes), and a destination file name of about 235 characters or more fails because the atomic-replace temporary name needs room in the same directory.

outputs_note: Rows are pipe-delimited `field|value` lines written one at a time via `ctx.write_output()`; there is no multi-row output for any of these three actions, and a validation or transport failure emits a single `error|<message>` line in place of the normal fields rather than a row with an error status. `download`'s four fields (`status|path|size|hash`) and `get`'s two fields (`status|body`, plus `truncated|<cap>` only when the body was cut) match their declared result columns exactly. `head`'s declared columns do **not** match what the code emits: the leg writes only `status` and a single `headers` field holding the full raw response header block (one `Name: value` pair per line, newline-joined, in the order the server sent them; before the cpp-httplib 0.59 bump the order was unspecified (hash order, differing by platform)) — `content_length` and `content_type` are declared in the definition YAML but never populated by `do_head`; see Caveats.

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result only.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore (90-day default retention, `response_store.hpp:153`), queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`.

**Not consumed by** daily-sync inventory, the Echo warehouse, DEX, or metrics — no server-side code references `agent.http_client.*` or `http_client` outside `agent_registry.cpp`'s instruction-catalogue description strings (`agent_registry.cpp:860-863`) and the capability declarations.

**Sensitivity.** `get`/`download` rows carry the fetched URL's response body verbatim, and `head`'s `headers` field carries the full raw response header block — whatever the remote endpoint returns rides through unfiltered, so a URL pointed at an internal system could surface usernames, credentials, or other personal data in the body/headers; the `path`/`hash` fields otherwise carry nothing beyond the operator-chosen destination.
**Siblings:** none — no other plugin performs outbound HTTP.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) → `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) → `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("agent.http_client.get")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`.
